rationale: The prime job (scheduler.debounce coroutine) rebuilt the shared paint_pattern from empty over about 18 scheduler ticks, and Paint saved whatever was built so far; the still-pending job then called show_unsaved_grid again, re-showing the preview after the paint. The build is now a function returning a fresh table: the preview job calls it with coroutine.yield, and Paint calls it with a no-op yield so it always saves the complete primed pattern (same fader values and shift). The job also re-checks that the prime is still armed before showing the preview, so a job overtaken by Paint (or Cancel) no longer re-shows it. The scheduler is unchanged.
oracle: README 424 (prime shows the algorithm's potential steps; painting deactivates the dimly blinking overlaps) and README 428 (pressing prime again paints your edits): a paint must apply the full primed exclusive-or on all 64 cells and the preview must not return.
